1.why: Sans-serif typeface with clear headings, adequate line spacing and high contrast dark-on-light text is used consistently across all five screens, though the monospace secret block is tightly set.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used and most text is short, but step 04/05 includes a dense four-line 'Evaluation behavior' paragraph that approaches a block of text.

3.why: The layout is a single narrow centred card that would reflow acceptably on a phone, but the screenshots are rendered at desktop width and the long secret string plus wide log panel risk cramping/overflow at mobile size.

4.why: Headings and banners are short and plain, yet the authenticator step uses technical wording ('Time-based / TOTP', 'deterministic evaluation secret', '30-second windows') that is not plain language.

5.why: Only the phone field shows a placeholder example (+1 555 010 0184); the verification code and six-digit authenticator fields show no example format, only a mock code line.

6.why: Most steps need only a sentence, but to complete enrolment the user must read the multi-sentence 'Evaluation behavior' explanation to know what to do with the secret.

7.why: The manual setup secret JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP is displayed in a plain read-only box with no copy button or copy affordance, so it must be transcribed by hand.

8.why: No QR code or scan option is offered anywhere; the step is explicitly labelled 'Manual setup secret' only.

9.why: Standard text inputs are present but there is no visible indication of autofill/one-time-code support, and the instruction 'Do not save it in this browser' actively discourages password-manager use.

10.why: Each screen has a single bold title and one prominent blue primary button, though no step indicator (e.g. 'Step 2 of 4') shows where the user is in the flow.

11.why: Most screens ask one action, but step 04/05 combines adding the secret to an app and entering a code, and step 03 presents both 'Set up authenticator' and a red 'Sign out' button.

12.why: Status is conveyed mainly via a developer log panel and a terse badge; after the failed activation the only feedback is 'Verification could not be completed.' with no statement of what happened next or what to do.

13.why: The user can retry the code entry and go 'Back to settings', but there is no reveal/hide toggle, no re-request or regenerate secret option, and no recovery codes are ever issued (count stays at 0).

14.why: 'Verification could not be completed.' names neither the specific problem nor any remedy, giving no guidance on clock drift, expiry, or re-entry.

15.why: No countdown timer is visible, but the identity code is stated to expire in five minutes and the TOTP is bound to 30-second windows, so time pressure is imposed rather than generous.
